issues.desc: checklist CHK-006 context lists the six registration files as registry.ts (MAIN_TOOLS), cli/command-catalog.ts, core/command-policy.ts, core/config.ts, core/process-fact-levels.ts, core/process-fact-registry.ts. Verified against source: the MAIN_TOOLS array is actually declared and exported at packages/main/src/cli/command-catalog.ts:228 (export const MAIN_TOOLS: ToolDef[] = [...]), and re-exported by cli-engine.ts (import { MAIN_TOOLS } from ./cli/command-catalog.js; export { MAIN_TOOLS };) -- NOT defined in registry.ts. registry.ts is a separate mechanism (createMainRegistry / registerBatch, the handler-dispatch table); it is a genuinely required registration point (confirmed by packages/main/src/tasks/command-ownership-contract.ts:136, which checks that MAIN_TOOLS-listed commands have a registered handler in createMainRegistry -- a DISPATCHABILITY check, not the MAIN_TOOLS schema definition itself), but the parenthetical (MAIN_TOOLS) attached to registry.ts implies the MAIN_TOOLS array/schema lives there, which is incorrect and could send an implementer looking in the wrong file for the MAIN_TOOLS catalog entry.

background.md Solution Tradeoffs and checklist CHK-008 context describe the three enumeration arrays in scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs near :1013, :1229, :1265 uniformly as MAIN_TOOLS command-name enumeration arrays. Verified against source: only the array at line 1013 (inside assertProofStoryProgressiveBoundary) is actually checked against MAIN_TOOLS/cli/command-catalog.ts (assert message literally reads CLI schema: ProofStory command missing from MAIN_TOOLS: dollar-commandName, checked via catalogText.includes(name colon commandName)). The array at line 1229 (same function) is checked against core/command-policy.ts entries instead (assert message ProofStory pre-DEV command missing policy: commandName, using commandPolicyPath). The array near line 1265 lives inside a different function, assertProofStoryGateConsumedFacts (starts line 1260); it is actually const commands = [ at line 1263 with the loop trigger for (const commandName of commands) at line 1277 -- not itself an inline for-of over an array literal the way the other two are -- and is checked against core/process-fact-levels.ts plus core/process-fact-registry.ts (levelRegistry/registry), not MAIN_TOOLS. Calling all three MAIN_TOOLS arrays is imprecise: two of the three validate different registries (command-policy.ts and process-fact-levels/registry.ts respectively) -- though the cited line numbers do still land inside the correct enumeration for adding the new command in each case.

background.md Conversational Texture uses the workstream code W2c (the section 1.1.3 binding-freeze rule ... lands with the chain in W2c) without ever defining what W2c refers to. W2a is glossed inline via the Trigger Event paragraph (story B-c054, RFC 8785 CANON plus fail-closed policy resolver) and W2b is this story per index.json description (Second implementation leaf, W2b), but W2c appears nowhere else in background.md, index.json, or checklist.json and has no gloss, so a fresh reader cannot determine which future story or spec area W2c denotes.
